profile_text.body:
Scoir describes itself as a college and career network connecting students, guardians, counselors, middle schools, high schools, and colleges, with the stated goal of expanding college access and improving student outcomes. Its site presents the platform as a unified college planning network for finding the right fit, with tools for college and career discovery, application support, and college admissions counseling. It also offers an electronic document delivery system that the company says combines data and intelligence to save time and improve accuracy.

The company's tracked product is also named Scoir, listed under education and research AI, with career matching as its AI feature. It is used for college and career planning by students in grades 6 to 12, counselors, and families. The vendor states it does not sell student personal information. Pricing is free for students and families, while school plans are billed per student plus $250 setup, with a 50% discount per free or reduced lunch student.

The site includes customer testimonials, among them a claim that 92% of one school's Class of 2024 seniors applied to at least four colleges and 70% matriculated to four-year institutions. No lawsuits, MCP servers, or SEC or patent facts are recorded for Scoir.
